newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Protesters scuffle with Israeli soldiers in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Protesters scuffle with Israeli soldiers in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli police arrested 10 Palestinian and Israeli left-wing demonstrators in Hebron after scuffles erupted as protesters made their way to a site holy to both Moslems and Jews, witnesses said on Saturday.

The protesters, led by Israeli Arab parliament member Hashem Mahameed, were heading towards the Tomb of the Patriarchs where Jews had gathered for the annual reading of a biblical passage they regard as their birthright to the West Bank town.
"We came here to demonstrate in support of peace. What kind of government, which calls itself a government of peace, beats up Israeli parliament members and Palestinian old men?" Mahameed said.
Israeli soldiers, police and demonstrators shoved and hit one another with their fists while Jewish settlers watched, witnesses said.
Israeli military sources said scuffles broke out after left-wing demonstrators including members of the Meretz party and local Palestinians tried to hold a protest without proper permits.
The sources said the left-wing protesters had earlier tried to make their way to the Tomb of the Patriarchs, which is closed until this evening to Moslems for prayer.
"Meretz activists and Palestinians illegally gathered in a square near the Tomb of the Patriarchs where they threw stones at police, lightly injuring one officer," Israeli military sources said.
The Tomb of the Patriarchs in Hebron, traditionally the site bought by Abraham, is now a complex revered by both Jews and Moslems. It is known to Moslems as the al-Ibrahimi Mosque.
In February 1994 Baruch Goldstein, a Jewish militant from Kiryat Arba settlement adjacent to Hebron, shot dead 29 Arabs at prayer in the mosque. He was beaten to death by survivors.

Security was heightened in the town as thousands of observant Jews joined the 400-strong settler community for the reading of the Bible portion relating to Abraham's purchase of a burial area in Hebron for his wife.

Earlier in the day, Israeli Internal Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said Israel would detain dozens of Jewish militants who might actively oppose a turnover of Hebron ahead of an Israeli troop redeployment there.

Kahalani, asked about Jewish militants who oppose an Israeli troop withdrawal from most of Hebron, told Israel army radio: "We are preparing for a situation where extremists like this will open fire and will try to incite the flames.
"We are prepared for this situation and we will pick up those who are dangerous and endanger public life in the area and put them in some corner and take care of this matter."

Asked if he was referring to administrative detention orders which would allow security forces to imprison Jewish militants without trial, he said: "If we need to we will also do that. We have to prevent them from trying to incite the flames."
"There can be no peace while settlers, the brothers and sisters of Goldstein remain in Hebron," MP Mahameed said.
Israel and the PLO are locked in U.S.-brokered negotiations on implementing a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the town of 100,000 Palestinians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the Likud Party seeks to modify the Hebron deal signed by the previous Labour-led government to safeguard the settlers who live in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes to the deal.
